reading.body:
Vantage WA11 is one building in a three-building campus in Quincy, Washington totaling 89 MW of critical IT load and 775,000 square feet, though the operator does not publish how that capacity divides among the three buildings. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, the 89 MW campus-wide figure would correspond to roughly 2,200 racks, but WA11's individual share is not stated. The campus ranks third among Washington state's 46 mapped data center facilities by published capacity and represents nearly the entire 60 MW of publicly disclosed capacity in the state.

WA11 holds Tier III certification, qualifying it for three concurrent maintenance windows without downtime to critical systems. The building also carries LEED Gold status, indicating it meets energy efficiency standards but not specifying renewable energy sourcing. Neither certification reveals what workloads the operator markets to tenants or whether the campus is currently fully leased.

The lack of building-level capacity breakdown leaves WA11's actual scale within the campus opaque. Washington's grid position and hydropower access have made it a significant draw for data center operators in recent years, but the state publishes minimal detailed capacity data, making this campus one of very few facilities there with any disclosed figure at all.
